reason: Three material, repairable construction errors remain. The builder keys rows on COMPLEX_ID_NUM, a BSEE complex/group identifier, so it is not one row per structure and silently drops 102 eligible structures; the authority filter never evaluates AUTHORITY_TYPE='OCS Lease' and instead accepts any non-null SURF_LEASE_NUM while ignoring the actual L/R/E/T/S authority codes, with a complex-level 5,825-to-6,600 fan-out; and the isolated_rows/independence claim rests on unique IDs plus a post-hoc drop_duplicates, so split membership is determined by an earliest-record selection rather than the stated structure cohort. Target direction (removal within 25 years), the 68 ft median depth unit check, the fixed 1986-2000 split boundaries, and the U.S. public-domain licence basis are otherwise sound. No label-derived group-rate feature is present in the supplied builder, so the specific later-rate-update leak is not demonstrated, but any area/district base-rate reference must be train-only and closed-window.

findings.issue: The row key is a complex/group identifier, not a structure identifier, so the dataset is not one row per structure and 102 eligible structures are silently deleted.
findings.evidence: source-checks.json reports structure_id='COMPLEX_ID_NUM', id_column='COMPLEX_ID_NUM', eligible_rows=1961, distinct_ids=1859 and duplicates_consolidated=102. BSEE FieldDefinitions defines COMPLEX_ID_NUM as 'The unique identifier assigned to a single man-made structure or a group of structures connected by a walkway' and STRUCTURE_NUMBER as 'A unique number assigned to a specific structure within a complex' (https://www.data.bsee.gov/Platform/PlatformStructures/FieldDefinitions.aspx). BSEE's Offshore Infrastructure Dashboard identifies a structure as 'Complex ID – Structure Number' (https://www.bsee.gov/what-we-do/environmental-compliance/decommissioning/offshore-infrastructure-dashboard/oid-layout-and-instructions). The 'one row per structure' check only verifies out[ID].is_unique after drop_duplicates, and the 0.948 cardinality check measures complex uniqueness, so neither detects the structure collapse.
findings.repair: Build structure_id from COMPLEX_ID_NUM plus STRUCTURE_NUMBER (for example '10203-A'), require that composite to be unique before splitting, and do not drop the 102 distinct structures. Re-run the cohort, label, split and feature-coverage checks on the structure-level key.

findings.issue: The authority filter does not implement the declared AUTHORITY_TYPE='OCS Lease' population; it uses an undecoded lease-number proxy and joins on complex ID.
findings.evidence: In construction_code._lease_id_set the code searches only for literal 'OCS'/'LEASE' substrings; the actual PLTFRM_ATH_TYPE values are single letters, so that returns None. construction_code._authority_member then falls back to any non-null SURF_LEASE_NUM that is not flagged by SN_ROW_FK/SN_RUE_FK. source-checks.json records source='authority member lease number, PlatStrucRawData/mv_platstruc_authorityhist.txt', distinct_values=['L','R','E','T','S'], structures_with_lease_authority=5825, while the cohort condition oc_lease_authority=6600. BSEE FieldDefinitions lists AUTHORITY_TYPE values 'OCS Lease, State Lease, Right-of-Way, Right-of-Use and Easement or Time Extension' (https://www.data.bsee.gov/Platform/PlatformStructures/FieldDefinitions.aspx), so a non-null SURF_LEASE_NUM does not establish OCS lease status. The 5,825-to-6,600 fan-out is consistent with joining authority on complex rather than structure.
findings.repair: Resolve authority at the structure level using COMPLEX_ID_NUM plus STRUCTURE_NUMBER, decode and validate PLTFRM_ATH_TYPE (or read AUTHORITY_TYPE where available), and filter exactly 'OCS Lease', excluding State Lease, Right-of-Way, Right-of-Use and Easement, and unrelated Time Extension records. Report counts by authority type and by join cardinality.

findings.issue: The isolated_rows/independence claim is based only on unique row IDs and is not established; the dedup step is a non-random selection that can remove later structures from their assigned chronological split.
findings.evidence: evaluation_contract.cross_row_audit.rationale says 'Each structure contributes one independent row with a unique identifier and disjoint installation-date cohort windows.' The code does out.sort_values([ID, TIME, '_completeness'], ascending=[True, True, False]).drop_duplicates(subset=[ID], keep='first'). For a complex with structures installed in different cohort years, only the earliest/most complete structure is retained; the later structure and its eval/holdout membership are deleted. The task's simple_references also call for a 'base rate by structure type, OCS area and district', i.e. label-derived group statistics; the supplied builder computes no such rate and implements no train-only/closed-window restriction.
findings.repair: Use the structure-level key and either retain every structure or define an explicit complex-level cohort. Audit shared block/field/area membership across splits. If any area/district/type base-rate reference is materialized, compute it only from training rows whose 25-year outcome window closed before the scored row's installation date, and document that rule.

limitations: Current-vintage snapshot: install-time availability of static attributes and authority status is assumed, not proven by a historical snapshot.
The L/R/E/T/S values of PLTFRM_ATH_TYPE are not decoded; possible State Lease contamination is indicated but not quantified.
Removal-date completeness and full 25-year observation of every retained structure were not independently verified; the follow-up check proves only that the latest cutoff is <= 2026-01-01.
SURF_N_S_DIST and SURF_E_W_DIST units are assumed feet; install month/day precision is weak and year-only dates become January.

The evaluation runner is supplied only as file hashes, so its feature whitelist and any area/district/type reference baselines cannot be verified; no label-derived group-rate column exists in the supplied builder, so the specific later-rate-update leak is not demonstrated.
The fixed-horizon rule labels structures not removed by their cutoff as 0 even if removed later.
The licence basis is U.S. federal public information and 17 U.S.C. § 105; no worldwide dedication is asserted, which is not a blocker for these U.S. records.
Measured metrics are on the stated 571 evaluation rows; no uncertainty interval and no universal performance ceiling should be inferred.
